alt: Two grids side by side. The left one is the source after a transpose. Each of its rows is highlighted in turn and copied, reversed, into the same row of the right grid, which ends as the source rotated 90 degrees clockwise.

steps.caption: Step one is already done: transposing the 2-by-3 source gives this 3-by-2 grid on the left. Step two reverses each of its rows, filling the result on the right.
Row 0 of the transposed grid is 1, 4. It reads backward in the result. Result row 0 is 4, 1.
Row 1 of the transposed grid is 2, 5. It reads backward in the result. Result row 1 is 5, 2.
Row 2 of the transposed grid is 3, 6. It reads backward in the result. Result row 2 is 6, 3.
Every row is reversed. The result is the source rotated 90 degrees clockwise: the source's top-left value 1 is now in the top-right corner, at row 0, column 1.
